headline: Markets pause pre-payrolls after ADP miss eases hike fears
body: Equities enter Friday in wait-and-see mode ahead of the August nonfarm payrolls report, the data point that's repeatedly swung Fed rate-hike expectations this week. Wednesday's ADP print showed private payrolls up just 38,000, the weakest reading since January, and stocks rallied into Thursday's close — the Dow's best day in about a month (+1.2%), with the S&P 500 (+1%) and Nasdaq (+1.4%) close behind — as long yields eased and Fed Governor Christopher Waller signaled openness to holding rates steady if inflation cooperates. Even so, CME-implied odds of a September hike only slipped to roughly 62%, and today's Fear & Greed reading sits at 45, moderate fear rather than the exuberance a multi-day rally might suggest. Consensus for August payrolls calls for a rebound to 53,000-65,000 jobs with unemployment near 4.1%, a print likely to move the rate debate more than recent price action has.

Retail chatter today reads as earnings-driven rather than macro-driven, with no single dominant story. WallStreetBets mentions skew toward mega-cap AI names — Google, Amazon, and Apple carry a bullish tilt — while Broadcom and Nvidia are seeing sharp spikes in mention volume tied to chip and AI-infrastructure momentum. On Stocktwits, the trending tickers are earnings-specific and mixed in tone: Planet Labs is drawing both bullish backlog-growth commentary and skepticism over soft next-quarter guidance; Campbell Soup has traders split between bears citing a dividend cut and weak outlook and contrarians eyeing the depressed valuation; HPE is trading higher on a clean beat-and-raise tied to AI infrastructure demand. Taken together, this looks less like a coordinated risk-on or risk-off push and more like a market digesting scattered single-stock surprises while the bigger directional question — how the labor data lands — stays unresolved until the numbers print.
